planting.note: Plant container stock in spring against a shaded fence, trellis, or north-facing wall; Henry's honeysuckle climbs by twining and needs support to train upward.

directions: Plant against a shaded fence, trellis, or north-facing wall in part shade; Henry's honeysuckle is an evergreen-to-semi-evergreen twining vine valued for thriving where most flowering vines struggle, since it tolerates significant shade while still producing yellow-and-purple tubular flowers followed by black berries. Its narrow spread of only about 2-3 feet but tall climbing habit of 9-18 feet makes it a good choice for softening a vertical shaded surface without sprawling into nearby beds. Provide a sturdy support for the twining stems to climb and prune lightly after flowering to control size.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring against a sheltered wall or fence in shade to part shade; Himalayan holboellia can take a cool north-facing wall in full shade.

directions: Plant against a sheltered wall or fence in shade to part shade; Himalayan holboellia is a vigorous evergreen twining vine with leathery, purple-tinged leaves that provide year-round structure, unusual for a shade-tolerant climber. Fragrant flowers in spring give way to edible, sausage-shaped purple fruit, a genuine bonus on an ornamental vine. It reaches 13-26 feet with an 8-13 foot spread given a sturdy support, and tolerates a cool north wall in full shade better than most flowering vines, though it needs winter protection outside zones 8-11.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring against a sheltered wall or trellis in part shade to full sun; give it protection from hard freezes outside the mildest zones.

directions: Plant against a sheltered wall or trellis in part shade to full sun; this evergreen twining climber reaches 16-23 feet with leathery, five-to-nine-leaflet foliage, and bears heavily fragrant, pale-yellow flowers flushed purple in late spring followed by edible lilac-purple sausage-shaped fruit. It is damaged by hard freezes below roughly 23°F, so site it in a protected microclimate at the colder end of its zone 8-11 range. Give it room to climb and a sturdy support, since the vigorous twining growth will quickly cover a trellis or pergola once established.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring against a sturdy support in part shade; this is a dioecious vine, so female plants need a male nearby to set the ornamental purple berries.

directions: Plant against a sturdy pergola, arbor, or large trellis in part shade, with some afternoon shade appreciated in hot climates; Sinofranchetia chinensis is a vigorous deciduous twining vine, the sole species in its genus, reaching 30-50 feet where given room to climb. White flower racemes appear in late spring, and on female plants pendant, grape-like purple berries follow in fall, though the vine is dioecious and needs both a male and female plant present to fruit. It is dormant-hardy to roughly -20°F, making it tougher than many evergreen shade vines, but needs ample space to accommodate its eventual size.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring against a wall or trellis the self-clinging tendrils can grip; like other Parthenocissus species it tolerates considerable shade though fall color is often more vivid with some sun.

directions: Plant against a wall, fence, or trellis in part shade to part sun; Thomson's Virginia creeper is a deciduous woody climber with five-leaflet palmate foliage that emerges reddish-purple and turns bright red in autumn, climbing to around 30 feet by self-clinging tendrils. Like its better-known relatives it tolerates shaded sites well, though the strongest fall color develops with at least some direct sun during the growing season. It needs no training once established against a suitable climbing surface and requires only occasional pruning to keep it within bounds.
sources: Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center reference

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring against a trellis or as a groundcover in part shade, with protection from the hottest afternoon sun; Pink Showers reblooms through summer unlike the plain white species form.

directions: Plant against a trellis or use as a groundcover in part shade, with some protection from the hottest afternoon sun; Pink Showers is a star jasmine selection with glossy evergreen foliage and fragrant, light-pink, star-shaped flowers that rebloom intermittently through summer rather than flowering only once in spring like the common white-flowered species. It reaches about 10 feet tall and 4 feet wide over five years when trained as a climber, or can be kept lower and wider as a groundcover. It shares the species' general cold hardiness, performing reliably in zones 8-10.

planting.note: Plant in autumn with roots shaded and cool and the top growth in brighter light, in sharp, well-drained soil; Lansdowne Gem is one of the deepest-colored winter clematis selections.

directions: Plant in autumn with the roots shaded and cool while the bronze-tinted, deeply incised evergreen foliage climbs into brighter light above, in sharp, well-drained soil. Lansdowne Gem was selected by New Zealand plantsman Michael Jerard in 1995 and bears claret-red, bell-shaped flowers with creamy anthers from November through February, among the deepest-colored of the winter-flowering clematis selections. Like other Clematis cirrhosa cultivars it flowers when little else is in bloom, making it valuable for off-season color on a sheltered wall or fence. Prune only lightly right after flowering, since next winter's buds form soon afterward.

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container transplants in spring or early fall in moist, well-drained soil in shade to full sun; Gold Heart's gold center variegation holds best with at least some light.

directions: Plant rooted cuttings or nursery transplants in moist, well-drained soil in shade to full sun, where trailing or climbing stems root as they travel to form a dense evergreen cover. Gold Heart carries small, dark-green leaves boldly splashed gold at the center, holder of a Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit for its reliable variegation and vigor. Given support it self-clings and climbs to 13 feet or more, or it can be left to sprawl as a groundcover; like the species, it is considered invasive across much of the eastern United States and Pacific Northwest, so check local regulations before planting outdoors.

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container transplants in spring in moist, well-drained soil in shade to part shade; variegation holds best with some light rather than the deepest shade.

directions: Plant rooted cuttings or nursery transplants in moist, well-drained soil in shade to part shade; Creme de Menthe is a Japanese ivy selection with narrow, glossy, blue-green leaves edged in creamy white, staying notably compact at about 30 inches whether grown as a short climber or low groundcover. It is a more restrained, slower-spreading alternative to English ivy for gardeners wanting variegated evergreen groundcover without the aggressive spread associated with Hedera helix. Give it a sheltered spot with some light to keep the variegation crisp, and water regularly through its first season to establish.
